item.text: {"facts":[{"source_id":"SRC-52801fa335d7c857","start_unit":3,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"Egypt’s government jointly signed the 2023–2027 UN Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework in May 2023; the UN Country Team reported delivering more than US$209 million of activities in Egypt during 2023 across human capital, economic development, climate resilience, governance, and women’s empowerment, and partnered with the government on an Integrated National Financing Strategy.","question_ids":["5B.1","5B.6","6B.1","6B.2","8B.2","8B.6"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"Directly concerns 2023 and the 2023–2027 framework; implementation and outcomes are reported collectively by the UN rather than attributed exclusively to el-Sisi.","ruler_attribution":"The government jointly signed the framework and partnered on the financing strategy, but the report does not establish el-Sisi’s personal direction or causal responsibility.","limitations":["Collective UN activity is not equivalent to ruler-controlled implementation.","The supplied excerpt provides no quantified outcome results for Egypt’s population."]},{"source_id":"SRC-120e759ca627a090","start_unit":2,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"A UN Working Group on Arbitrary Detention reported a pattern in Egypt of re-imprisoning people subjected to enforced disappearance or continuously detaining them on fabricated political charges, with torture during disappearance; it said the pattern raised concern about a systemic problem and that Egypt’s government did not respond to its communication concerning ten cases.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.2","3B.4","3B.5","3B.9","4B.3","4B.4","4B.9","7B.2","7B.7"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The Working Group opinion was dated 27 September 2023 and was reported in November 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The finding concerns Egyptian state authorities during el-Sisi’s presidency; the excerpt does not document a personal order by el-Sisi.","limitations":["The report is conveyed through Mada Masr and civil-society organizations rather than reproduced in full.","The Working Group opinion is not described as binding in Egyptian courts."]},{"source_id":"SRC-abfe886eeb2ad714","start_unit":5,"end_unit":5,"fact_summary":"An Egyptian press-freedom monitoring report recorded 29 violations against journalists and media workers during July–September 2023, including seven pretrial-detention renewal cases, three arbitrary arrests, three incidents of verbal assault or threats, and additional cases involving financial rights, arbitrary dismissal, property seizure, content removal, defamation, physical assault, and property damage.","question_ids":["3B.8","4B.3","4B.6","4B.9"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Directly covers the third quarter of 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The report evaluates violations and the performance of Egyptian governing institutions regulating journalism; it does not establish that el-Sisi personally ordered each violation.","limitations":["The supplied excerpt does not identify individual perpetrators or adjudicated findings for each incident.","The monitor is an independent Egyptian research and rights organization, not a court."]},{"source_id":"SRC-2108324f89dbfe0f","start_unit":4,"end_unit":5,"fact_summary":"In August 2023, el-Sisi stated that the government was pursuing an economic plan to reduce imports, produce domestic substitutes, expand cultivated land, secure foreign currency, and maintain a strategic reserve of basic commodities for five to six months; he said more than three million feddans would be added to Egypt’s agricultural map in the coming months, while acknowledging continued dependence on imported wheat, maize, cooking oil, fuel, industrial inputs, and medicines.","question_ids":["5B.1","5B.6","5B.9","5B.10","8B.1","8B.2"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Statements and plans were reported on 20 August 2023; some agricultural expansion was prospective rather than completed during the period.","ruler_attribution":"The source directly attributes the stated priorities and targets to el-Sisi.","limitations":["The excerpt reports announced plans and claimed efforts, not verified execution or outcomes.","The source provides no independent assessment of the reserve or land-expansion claims."]},{"source_id":"SRC-2108324f89dbfe0f","start_unit":5,"end_unit":5,"fact_summary":"El-Sisi said Egypt hosted a Conference of Sudan’s Neighboring States as part of an effort to find a peaceful solution to Sudan’s crisis and characterized Egypt’s foreign policy as moderate, balanced, and non-interventionist.","question_ids":["2B.1","2B.7","2B.10","8B.9"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"The statement concerns Egypt’s 2023 diplomatic response to the Sudan crisis.","ruler_attribution":"The source directly attributes the diplomatic posture and hosting decision to el-Sisi.","limitations":["The excerpt does not assess whether the conference produced a durable settlement or reduced violence.","The account is a report of el-Sisi’s own statement."]},{"source_id":"SRC-caf90f157d1136ae","start_unit":2,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"UNICEF’s 2023–2027 Egypt country-program assessment reported that government programs had expanded basic services, social-service access, and protection for families in need, while nearly 30% of Egyptians lived in poverty, with substantially higher rates in parts of Upper Egypt.","question_ids":["6B.1","6B.2","6B.3","6B.10","5B.8"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The assessment was published in January 2023 and covers the 2023–2027 country program.","ruler_attribution":"The assessment attributes the programs to the Egyptian government collectively, not specifically to el-Sisi.","limitations":["The supplied text does not quantify the programs’ budgets, uptake, or causal effects.","The poverty estimate is a national-level finding and does not isolate 2023 changes."]},{"source_id":"SRC-caf90f157d1136ae","start_unit":3,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"UNICEF reported that fewer than one quarter of children were enrolled in public pre-primary education; at least one million school-age children with disabilities and many refugee and migrant children were out of school; and children continued to face violence, exploitation, abuse, neglect, and harmful practices including female genital mutilation.","question_ids":["6B.2","6B.3","6B.8","6B.10","3B.7"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The findings appear in UNICEF’s January 2023 country-program assessment for the 2023–2027 period.","ruler_attribution":"The findings concern conditions and protection gaps under the Egyptian government’s jurisdiction; the excerpt does not attribute them to a personal el-Sisi directive.","limitations":["The excerpt does not provide year-on-year trends or identify which level of government is responsible for each gap.","It does not quantify the prevalence of every listed harmful practice."]},{"source_id":"SRC-caf90f157d1136ae","start_unit":3,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"UNICEF reported that girls and young women were disproportionately affected by the transition from education to work, with female unemployment three times the male rate, and identified a mismatch between school-acquired skills and employer requirements.","question_ids":["5B.4","5B.8","6B.3","6B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The finding is contained in the January 2023 UNICEF country-program assessment.","ruler_attribution":"The source describes national labor-market conditions and does not establish el-Sisi’s personal responsibility for the skills mismatch or unemployment gap.","limitations":["The excerpt does not state the absolute unemployment rates or their precise reference year.","It does not evaluate specific government employment measures."]},{"source_id":"SRC-4516abc636132946","start_unit":6,"end_unit":7,"fact_summary":"A June 2023 POMED report described el-Sisi’s New Administrative Capital as a US$58 billion, debt-fueled military-led megaproject and concluded that military-led megaproject spending had contributed to Egypt’s worst economic crisis in decades.","question_ids":["5B.1","5B.3","5B.6","5B.10","8B.1","8B.7","8B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Published 7 June 2023 and explicitly addresses the period of el-Sisi’s rule up to 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The report directly frames the project and spending pattern as el-Sisi’s initiative and political-economic program.","limitations":["The supplied excerpt summarizes the report rather than providing its underlying data tables.","The report’s characterization is an external analytical finding, not a judicial determination."]},{"source_id":"SRC-4516abc636132946","start_unit":7,"end_unit":7,"fact_summary":"POMED reported that, despite el-Sisi’s repeated assertion that the state would not pay for the New Administrative Capital, most funding came from public coffers; it also reported billions redirected to the military and regime-connected cronies through no-bid contracts while civilian-government debt increased.","question_ids":["5B.1","5B.3","5B.5","5B.6","7B.1","7B.9","8B.3","8B.6"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The report was published in June 2023 and describes financing and contracting practices during the project’s development.","ruler_attribution":"The report attributes the public financing model and project direction to el-Sisi’s administration, while the statement about his assertion concerns his public representation of the project’s financing.","limitations":["The supplied excerpt gives no contract-level amounts or names of beneficiaries.","The author is identified by a pseudonym because of sensitivity, limiting independent assessment of the research process."]}],"documents_with_no_material_fact":["SRC-4297b51f7b7369d3","SRC-49ba68347e38c382","SRC-835988c0e7045a6e","SRC-7831f84e22e787a9","SRC-5b4b07f3f5ebaa07","SRC-f6f44d1f47ea0226"],"batch_limitations":["The supplied excerpts for several documents were landing-page metadata or navigation rather than the substantive report contents.","Facts are limited to the 2023–2023 period and do not constitute scores."]}
